meta.contention_policy: raw/perf/calibrate ran on an exclusive box and is the authority for wall clock. Mapping/attribution slices ran with 3-5 sibling agents; their wall figures run 1.9-2.2x high and CPU up to 38% high. Execution-kind splits and stack-sample fractions are contention-robust and are taken from whichever slice measured them best.

verdict.answer: Yes, weighted by what a human waits on -- but the reason is parallelism and frequency, not the CPU split.

verdict.single_load_bearing_fact: The M1 decision-table fixpoint is 1,263 foreground wall-seconds/day (61% of everything a human waits on), is 100% this repo's own Python by leaf-module attribution, has ZERO native frames in a 25,410-leaf-sample call graph, and runs strictly single-threaded (337.66 CPU-s against 337.87 s wall).

frequency_basis.method: git log, last 80 commits over 9 active days, each commit's files classified by which gate closure they fall in. MEASURED by this slice; no other slice did this.
frequency_basis.assumed_not_measured: one refreshing cycle per artifact-arming commit; one settling (gate) pass per two refreshers; 2 verdict-only passes/day; 2 no-op passes/day
frequency_basis.sensitivity: Halving or doubling cycles-per-commit moves daily totals by ~40% but the rewritable FRACTION by under 2 points, because it scales the M1 and surface terms together.

contradictions.why: attr-overhead applied the bucket of an ISOLATED SINGLE-PROCESS sweep test to all 2,197 CPU-s. attr-tests sampled two LIVE xdist workers (68.15%/76.83%, 42,255 samples) and instrumented every one of 88,448,272 hb.shape calls (71.96%), then accounted for the prelude separately.
contradictions.consequence: attr-overhead's whole-system rewritable fraction of 55.37% is ~5 points low; corrected ~60%.

contradictions.claim: Review surface cold: 190.1 s / 136.7 CPU vs 130.9 s / 125.2 CPU serial vs 48.6 s / 196.9 CPU at j6 vs 35.6 s / 143.1 CPU at j6
contradictions.why: Identical command and identical output in every run (62,148 units / 292,098 rows / 36 batches). Contention inflated attr-surface's j6 CPU by 37.6% and wall by 36.7%.
contradictions.consequence: The serial-vs-parallel CPU gap (125.2 vs 143.1) is real, not contention: each spawn worker re-loads both fonts, the spec and six subset tables. --jobs 10 contended (67.8 s) is worse than --jobs 6 uncontended (35.6 s).

contradictions.claim: make review 47.0 s; gate:make-test skip 0.15 s; census 74.65 s wall
contradictions.why: The census's 74.65 s wall against 46.07 CPU-s is 62% utilisation -- the tell.
contradictions.consequence: Every mapping-slice wall figure needs a ~2x discount.

contradictions.claim: '37% of leaf samples are frozen-dataclass methods that slots=True would cut'
contradictions.adjudication: Half right; the actionable half is WRONG.
contradictions.why: The 36.95% is confirmed (<string> frames, with <string>:2 __init__ alone at 25.14% of Python-level leaves). But the same agent-family's own microbenchmark measures slots=True at 361.7 ns/construct against 375.4 ns without -- a 3.6% saving, not 37%.
contradictions.consequence: The 37% is recoverable only by NOT CONSTRUCTING the objects: a plain tuple is 32.0 ns (11.7x) and hashes at 21.2 ns vs 107.0 ns (5.0x). This is a REWRITE argument, not a slots argument.

contradictions.claim: 'gc.freeze()/gc.disable() is 13% of the M1 build, nearly free money'
contradictions.adjudication: Directionally right; the A/B offered as proof does not support it.
contradictions.why: Three interleaved reps: GC-on 103.17/81.80/85.63 CPU-s, GC-off 70.92/76.48/95.64 -- one rep has GC-OFF SLOWER by 12%. The 13% is a minimum-of-reps across a set with +-35% spread under contention.
contradictions.consequence: What holds it up is independent: two samples put the GC group at 14.79% and 12.92% of leaf samples, and 15,698 collections collect 12 objects. Contrast the font build's identical lever, cleanly measured at -12.14% with byte-identical OTFs.

contradictions.adjudication: Confirmed as a measurement (9.2x against calibrate's uncontended 77.51 s); REJECTED as a lever.
contradictions.why: The flags-off build produces a DIFFERENT artifact: 479,371 windows vs 682,842, 1,165 rules vs 2,667, 2,867 GSUB rules vs 7,024, 197 cells vs 204.
contradictions.consequence: Not the same computation done faster -- weaker semantics. Cannot be banked without changing what the font does.

contradictions.why: Boundary instrumentation: 1.626 s of this repo's ray-casting against 0.062 s of fontTools charstring execution (96.3% repo); its own sample shows 0.12% native.
contradictions.consequence: It is repo Python, and entirely off the wall critical path (mono workers finish at 1.2 s while senior workers run 8.1 s).

contradictions.why: Cumulative-under-a-call-site and leaf-stack-fraction measure different things.
contradictions.consequence: Both say it is the dominant call site. I use 84% for apportioning kernel 1.

contradictions.claim: Surface size 264.5 MB / 266.7 MiB / 279.7 MB / 253 MiB
contradictions.why: I verified the live tree with du: rebuild/out/review is 253 MiB = 265.3 MB.
contradictions.consequence: All four agree once units are normalised.

contradictions.adjudication: Different corpora; all agree on shape.
contradictions.why: glyph_data/*.yaml alone vs the full load_glyph_data equivalent vs the 18 rune files.
contradictions.consequence: Use 7.3x / 1.150 CPU-s per make all, and 7.7x / 0.040 s per fingerprint pass.

contradictions.claim: 'Python is not the bottleneck' (1.40x) vs 'Python is emphatically the bottleneck' (11-29x)
contradictions.adjudication: Both right about their own workload; the disagreement IS the finding.
contradictions.why: make test is 2,212 CPU-s but 205.6 wall-s (10.76x parallel) and fires on 6.3% of commits. The M1 fixpoint is 337.9 CPU-s AND 337.9 wall-s (1.00x) and fires on ~68%.
contradictions.consequence: Weight by what a human waits on and the answer is yes, 91.0% rewritable, 11.1x ceiling.

contradictions.claim: The six-config table stage costs 337.66 CPU-s
contradictions.why: /usr/bin/time -l on the same run: 360.01 s real / 356.62 user / 2.34 sys. The reported figure omits ~19 CPU-s and 22.1 wall-s of interpreter teardown freeing a 7.46 GB object graph.
contradictions.consequence: I carry the teardown explicitly; it is a cost a human waits through and no profiler attributes it to anything.

open_questions: gate:conform has never been measured end to end on any machine. My 336 s/pass is a DERIVED FLOOR from the 168 us/text marginal cost, excluding witness top-ups which were over half of the July artifact's 14,335,037 shaping runs. It carries 25% of the combined day.
The verdict plumbing chain's ~23 s and complaints' ~3 s are cited from artifact_cycle.py's docstring and have never been measured anywhere. They carry 208 s/day (5% of the foreground).
rebuild/out/cycle-timings.ndjson still does not exist. ONE `make artifact-cycle` closes both questions above and turns every commit-message-cited figure into a measured one on this hardware.

Nobody has measured whether a Rust settlement kernel actually gets 10x on THIS workload. The constant-factor microbenchmarks (11.7x construct, 5.0x hash, 18-36x TSV) and the memory model (46 B/memo key vs 257.3) support 10-40x; no port exists.

Can build_tables be parallelised at all? It is serial by design because the cross-config TraceShare must live in one process, and the share carried 1.3-2.0 M entries per recipient config on the cold run. A fast rewrite should re-ask whether the share still pays.

A rewrite competes against work avoidance that already shipped: the trace memo + share take the table stage 337.9 -> 194.9 s; the unit cache takes the surface 143.1 -> 13.5 CPU-s. What is left is the fresh slice, and twelve recent commits were spent shrinking exactly that.

--conform-horizon may be a cheaper lever than any rewrite for the largest background term (WHATNEXT.md names it). Likewise max_chars_after in the calt sweep: 1 + 46 + 46^2 = 2,163 after-combinations would fall to 47, a 46x cut in make test's 88.4 M shapes. Both are coverage decisions no language change can reach.
make review, make complaint-docket and make novelty-order have no green record, no skip proof and no attribution slice. make review alone re-derives everything for 21.4 s on every invocation.
